steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: On 18 September 1931, Japan used the "Mukden Incident" - an explosion on the Japanese-owned South Manchurian Railway - as a pretext to invade Manchuria, a region of northern China. Japan occupied the entire province and set up the puppet state of "Manchukuo" in February 1932. The League's response was slow, weak, and ultimately ineffective. | Key Fact: In October 1935, Italy invaded Abyssinia (modern Ethiopia), one of the few independent African nations. The League imposed economic sanctions on Italy but they were half-hearted and failed to stop the invasion. By May 1936, Italy had conquered Abyssinia. The crisis was the League's most humiliating failure and effectively destroyed it as a peacekeeping body. | Key Fact: The Great Depression that followed the 1929 Wall Street Crash

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain why the League failed to stop Japan in Manchuria. (4 marks) | How important was the Hoare-Laval Pact in destroying the League's credibility? (8 marks) | "The Abyssinian Crisis was the League's worst failure." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from the league in the 1930s, and one past-paper question.
